subject: Finly discovery recap — p95 latency targets & streaming concurrency
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Howard <alex.howard@finly.com>, Sara Li <sara.li@finly.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 17:15:00 -0700
Subject: Finly discovery recap — p95 latency targets & streaming concurrency

Hi Alex / Sara,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciated the thorough walkthrough of Finly's streaming use case. Below is a short recap of what we heard, the success criteria you called out, and proposed next steps. Please correct anything I got wrong.

Pain points / current bottlenecks:
- High tail latency on streaming completions: current p95 ~= 820ms (with spikes above 1s during peak). This impacts first-byte and overall UX.
- Concurrency needs: sustained ~100–120 concurrent streaming sessions during peak with brief spikes to ~200.
- Cold starts and KV/cache misses contributing to variability (your infra team mentioned some requests are hitting cold GPUs).
- Current stack: prototype on a managed hosted provider + internal inference for some sensitive workloads; you get inconsistent latency and limited ability to tune batching/quantization.

Success criteria (what success looks like):
- p95 end-to-end streaming response (first-byte + steady token generation) <= 350ms for typical requests (90–200 tokens).
- Sustained concurrency of 100 sessions with graceful degradation to 200 during spikes.
- Stable streaming first-byte latency ideally < 100ms; jitter minimized so UX shows predictable token flow.
- Maintain current model quality / few-shot behavior; cost target to be discussed in POC but prefer predictable unit economics.

Proposed next steps:
1) We’ll provision a short POC environment (Redwood Dedicated / Private option) to replay a sample of your traffic.
2) You to share a 1 hour sample of production traffic (anonymized) + representative request sizes and concurrency profile.
3) Aditya (cc'd) will scope a recommended config (batching, KV caching, quantization profile) and estimate resource footprint.
4) Schedule a technical session with your infra/SRE to discuss network paths, TLS termination, and GPU cold-start behavior.

Attachments: finly-reqs-aug2026.pdf (high-level POC checklist and data instructions).

Proposed meeting: Wed Sep 2, 2026 10:00am PT for the technical session — does that work?

Thanks,
—Marissa

Subject: Re: Finly discovery recap — p95 latency targets & streaming concurrency

Thanks Marissa — this is accurate and helpful. A few clarifications / additional data points from our side:

- The 820ms figure is averaged across several endpoints; our production trace shows p95 is ~820ms for 1k-token sessions, but for short (50–200 token) sessions p95 is closer to 620ms. Spikes to ~1.2s happen during model reloads / scale events.
- Concurrency: sustained 120 during business hours, typical spike profile: 120 -> 200 for 2–5 minutes when reports roll out.
- First-byte: users notice stuttering when initial token is delayed > 150ms; ideal goal is <100ms.
- We currently rely on an external managed LLM provider for most routing and fall back to our internal models for sensitive workflows — that hybrid setup is what causes complexity.

We can provide a 1-hour anonymized traffic dump (logs + sample requests). I'll put that in the Drive folder and share access to the SRE team.

Also open to the Wed Sep 2 session — Alex (SRE lead) and Sara (Product) will join. Good to have Aditya on the technical scoping call.
